key_insight: The paper turns Gaussian entanglement quantification into a convex-geometry optimization problem, enabling efficient bounds on entanglement, secret key, and communication rates for multimode quantum optical systems.
engineering_relevance: It provides computable, energy-constrained performance bounds for quantum communication pipelines using realistic Gaussian states, with algorithms suitable for benchmarking and system design.
method: Derives Gaussian-restricted relative entropy and Rains entanglement via an integral representation and matrix geometric means.
Uses a convex-majorization algorithm with explicit geometric convergence and polynomial bit-complexity for fixed rational covariance input.
Applies teleportation simulation, energy allocation, and passive-basis loss-core optimization to bound two-way assisted quantum/private communication rates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports controlled numerical integration, approximate convex subproblem solving, and worked two- and three-mode examples that compare the resulting bounds with achievable rates, including pure-loss benchmarks.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees are for Gaussian-restricted quantities and fixed rational covariance matrices; unrestricted entanglement still needs photon-number truncation and controlled approximation error.
paper_title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
